ca6509fb836f: Validation rules cannot see other records. That single limitation is why most Salesforce booking systems discover their conflicts a day late.
7b5809d03087: Double-booking is a timing problem. By the time anything in standard Salesforce can tell you the room is taken, the user has already chosen it, filled in the rest of the form, and moved on.

fffa6072599d: They all share the same shape: reject the user <t1>after</t1> the choice. Even a correct custom solution produces "that slot is taken, please try again," which is a worse experience than never offering the slot.
90de23bdc114: Duplicate rules tempt people, so here is the rule. Two bookings conflict when one starts before the other ends and ends after the other starts. A booking from 9:00 to 10:00 and one from 9:30 to 10:30 overlap by half an hour while sharing no identical field values. Any approach based on matching values will miss it every time.
151af163a212: Conflict and capacity are different problems
eff5fbe292ff: They often get treated as one thing.
87c685ffcc9c: Two things competing for a resource that holds one. A room, an interviewer, a vehicle.
788d0507c0a0: A resource that holds several. The question is how many are left. A class with twenty seats, a shift needing four nurses, a desk zone with sixty spaces.
16739d3b43ac: Treating a capacity resource as a conflict resource means you can never book the second person. Treating a conflict resource as capacity-of-one technically works but loses the counts you probably want to report on.
f102c7f43a19: Capacity across a whole team: booked of capacity per day, overbooked days ringed in orange.
5e905ea549f0: "Block it" is not always right. When somebody selects twelve dates and two of them clash, rejecting the whole submission is hostile. Useful systems offer a choice:
f738f2197b12: Refuse the save and report the clash. Right when every date matters.
e68956dd9475: Save the ten that are free, report the two that were not. Usually the humane default for bulk selection.
45aca84a16cc: Permit the overlap deliberately. Some businesses overbook on purpose.
853eaa43d12f: Live capacity counts on each slot, so the conflict is visible before anyone clicks.
e33bf186eed2: Every mechanism above operates at save time. The fix is to move the check to <t1>selection</t1> time: query what already exists when the calendar loads, draw it onto the grid, and never offer a slot that is gone. Save-time checks still run as a backstop for the genuine race condition where two people are looking at the same free slot, but they stop being the primary defense.
19ed1a967962: <t1>How MultiDatePick does it.</t1> It reads existing records when the calendar renders, shows taken slots as taken, counts capacity with a live booked of capacity badge, and checks for conflicts again on save. <t2>Conflict Behavior</t2> sets block, skip or allow. In a Screen Flow, the <t3>Conflict Dates</t3> and <t4>Successful Bookings Count</t4> outputs tell the next screen exactly what happened.
